verdict.reasoning: Patient states chest has been tight for about three hours: 'my chest has been feeling really tight' and later 'for about... three hours now.'
Patient reports 'a little bit short of breath' and 'I'm feeling a bit wheezy, as well.'

Patient says, 'I had a cold last week... I had a sore throat, I had a runny nose... Are you feeling better now, other than the tight chest?' and 'the runny nose isn't as bad any more... but the cough's kind of stuck around.'

Chest tightness not pain: 'you wouldn't say you've got chest pains? ... It's more of a tight chest?' Patient: 'No, not really pain, it's more like, tight.' Worse with stairs and no SOB at rest: 'It does when I'm walking up stairs, I do feel like... more short of breath' and 'I'm definitely not short of breath at rest... No, no, no I'm not.'
Patient is worried about severe asthma recurrence: 'I just don't wanna have to get, um, that, that intubation again.'

History of asthma and severe exacerbation with intubation in adolescence: 'Yeah, yeah, I have asthma' and 'when I was in high school, I had to have a tube put down my throat.' Age 16–17: Patient says 'I think I was like seventeen. Sixteen maybe.'

Atopy history: 'I have like, a hayfever, you know, and some allergies just to dust' and 'my mum has eczema... when I was young, I also had eczema. And I had a milk protein allergy, when I was young too.'
Uses salbutamol as reliever: 'you know the um, uh, Ventolin. It's called uh, Salbutamol. I got that one' and doctor plans 'Ventolin as a PRN... when you need to.'

Uses Clenil (beclomethasone) but ran out about a week ago: 'then I have a steroid, a Clenil, Clenil inhaler' and 'they ran out and I, I forgot to, go and grab the next one... About a week ago.' Doctor confirms: 'you haven't got any Clenil, or any Ventolin at the moment?' Patient: 'Not with me right now, no, I ran out.'
No drug allergies: Doctor asks, 'any drug allergies, that you know of?' Patient: 'No, no, not allergic to anything. Just like, just the, dust and stuff, but nothing, no drugs.'
Patient mentions being at university: 'I was away at uni last week.' This supports that he is a university student.

Patient does not request a work note; instead doctor offers: 'I might give you some time off work as well... I think I would advise you just to, rest a little bit.' No request from the patient is documented.
Patient states: 'my mum has eczema.'
Patient states: 'my dad has asthma.'

Post-viral and medication lapse: patient had a cold last week and hasn’t used inhalers for about a week ('I was away at uni... I forgot to bring it with me... they ran out'). Symptoms: wheeze, non-productive cough, chest tightness, SOB on exertion and none at rest are all explicitly described in the transcript.

Patient has atopy (hay fever, dust allergy), but the transcript does not state that allergic rhinitis/atopy are currently contributing to this exacerbation; that causal linkage is an added interpretation not explicitly discussed.
Doctor plans to prescribe Ventolin and Clenil with a spacer: 'I would quite like to... get you some, uh, Ventolin, Clenil Modulite' and later, 'the other thing I'd like to send you is a spacer.'

Short course of oral steroids with side-effect counseling: 'give you a, dose of steroids... tablets which, um, you can take for five days. Uh, two tablets in the morning' and then discusses mood change, high blood sugar, rash, nausea, headaches.

Spacer technique and written instructions: 'I'll send you another one, and it has some instructions about how to use it, but essentially, uh, couple of puffs to prime it... breathing in and out, um, uh, for five or , five or ten breaths.'
Ventolin use threshold for seeking care: 'If you should start to use the Ventolin more than, uh, every three hours... it's a good idea to seek medical attention.'

Advised rest from work and self-certification: 'I might give you some time off work as well. You can self-certify first seven days, but uh, I think I would advise you just to, rest a little bit until you're feeling a bit better.'
Resume preventer and use Ventolin for wheeze: 'once you get better from this asthma attack, you can... use the Clenil Modulite in the morning, with Ventolin as a PRN... when you're getting wheezy.'
No discussion in the transcript of allergen avoidance advice or use of antihistamines or nasal steroids as part of this plan.

Red flag advice: 'Any deterioration in your symptoms, like worsening shortness of breath. Um, or just generally concerning symptoms, uh, pain in your chest tightness, uh, feeling light-headed... then, seek further medical attention anytime please.'
